<explanation>
Based on the file tree and README, this is a Laravel package that integrates various Large Language Model (LLM) providers into applications. It is structured as a library (package) to be installed via Composer in a Laravel (or PHP) application and provides extensive support for text generation, multi-step conversations, embeddings, structured outputs, and more. Here’s how you can craft a detailed system design diagram for this project:

1. Project Type & Purpose
   • This is a Laravel package (“Prism”) that abstracts integration with multiple AI/LLM providers.
   • Its purpose is to let developers easily generate text, manage tool-based interactions, and handle multi-step conversations within Laravel apps.
   • The README emphasizes it as a “powerful Laravel package” that simplifies working with LLMs while hiding the complexities of interacting with different providers.

2. Main Components to Include
   a. Core Package Components:
      - Core service classes (e.g., src/Prism.php, src/PrismManager.php, src/PrismServer.php)
      - Service Provider integration (src/PrismServiceProvider.php) for bootstrapping within the Laravel ecosystem.
      - Configuration Files (config/prism.php) that set up defaults for provider integrations and behaviors.
      
   b. Client-Facing Layers:
      - HTTP Controllers (src/Http/Controllers/PrismChatController.php and PrismModelController.php) that expose endpoints for interactions.
      - Facades (src/Facades/PrismServer.php, src/Facades/Tool.php) which provide a fluent interface.
      
   c. AI Provider Integrations:
      - A collection of provider-specific implementations under src/Providers (e.g., Anthropic, DeepSeek, Gemini, Groq, Mistral, Ollama, OpenAI, VoyageAI, XAI).
      - Within each provider folder, the pattern is similar: there are Concerns, Handlers, Maps, and ValueObjects. Illustrate that the package uses a common interface (in src/Contracts) to interact with all providers.
      
   d. Business Logic Components:
      - Text, Structured, and Embeddings logic are separated into their own directories (src/Text, src/Structured, src/Embeddings). Each handles requests, responses, steps, and builders for their respective functionalities.
      - Use of Schemas for structured validation (src/Schema classes).
      
   e. Support & Utilities:
      - Contracts defining interfaces (src/Contracts/Message.php, PrismRequest.php, Provider.php, Schema.php).
      - Concerns and Traits contained in src/Concerns for shared functionality.
      - Exceptions (src/Exceptions) for robust error handling across providers.
      - Enums (src/Enums) and Value Objects (src/ValueObjects) to enforce consistency in message formatting and metadata.

3. Relationships and Data Flow
   • The diagram should indicate that client requests are routed to HTTP Controllers that then call the core Prism components (Manager/Server).
   • The Prism Manager interacts with the configured provider implementations (selected from the Providers folder) via common contracts.
   • Data flows from the controllers → core logic (Prism/Manager) → provider-specific handlers → external API calls.
   • Results propagate back following the reverse path. Error handling occurs at both the provider level (via Exceptions) and within core logic.
   • Highlight dependency and invocation relationships among core components, providers, and helper classes (Concerns, ValueObjects, Schema).
   • There is also a testing suite verifying the integration between these pieces, as seen in the tests folder.

4. Architectural Patterns & Design Principles
   • The package follows a modular design, using the Strategy Pattern to manage multiple providers—each provider implementation conforms to a common interface.
   • Laravel’s Service Container is used for dependency injection (as indicated by the Service Provider and facades).
   • There’s a clear separation of concerns: HTTP layer, business/service layer, provider-specific logic, and utility components are clearly segmented.
   • Layered architecture: configuration layer (config/prism.php), business logic layer (src/*), and presentation/HTTP layer.

5. Diagram Guidelines Specific for This Laravel Package
   • Use blocks or shapes for each major component group:
        ▪ Laravel Integration (Service Provider, Facades, Controllers)
        ▪ Core Engine (Prism, PrismManager, PrismServer)
        ▪ Provider Abstraction (Contracts, Interfaces)
        ▪ Provider Implementations (folders such as Anthropic, DeepSeek, OpenAI, etc.)
        ▪ Domain-specific Logic (Text, Structured, Embeddings, Schemas)
        ▪ Error Handling & Utility Components (Exception classes, Enums, ValueObjects)
   • Draw directional arrows to show:
        ▪ How the client or application calls flow from HTTP Controllers to core engine components.
        ▪ The dispatch sequence from the core engine to the selected provider module (via Contract).
        ▪ The feedback loop from provider responses back to the application.
   • Use different colors or shapes to differentiate components (e.g., rectangles for core classes, rounded shapes for controllers, cylinders for external API services).
   • Label each component clearly with its file/directory name where possible (e.g., “PrismServiceProvider”, “Providers/OpenAI/OpenAI.php”).

6. Additional Elements to Include
   • External Services: Represent external LLM or AI provider services (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) as external nodes that the package communicates with.
   • Development & Testing Tools: Optionally show resources for tests, CI configurations (under .github/workflows), and documentation (docs folder) as supporting elements.
   • Configuration & Environment: Show the interplay between configuration files (config/prism.php) and the runtime environment.

7. Final Diagram Details
   • Ensure that each block/component has a clear label.
   • Use directional arrows to annotate the flow of data or method invocations.
   • Consider adding color coding or shapes to help distinguish between core components, provider integrations, and utility layers.
   • The diagram should capture as many essential elements of the architecture as possible without oversimplifying.

By following these guidelines, you will be able to produce a detailed and accurate system design diagram that reflects the modular architecture of "Prism" – a Laravel package that abstracts and integrates interactions with various LLM providers into a unified, easily extensible system. This clear mapping will help any developer or engineer quickly grasp the internal workings and extensibility points of the system. 

Happy diagramming!
</explanation>
